- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.

# Summary of the 2017 Manifesto

This document outlines a comprehensive political platform centered on completing Brexit negotiations and implementing domestic policy reforms across multiple sectors.

## Brexit and Trade

The manifesto establishes six key tests for Brexit success: restoration of parliamentary sovereignty free from European court jurisdiction, full migration control, reclaiming maritime rights up to 200 nautical miles, independent trade policy through the World Trade Organisation, no divorce payment to the EU, and completion by end of 2019. The document strongly advocates for restoring the fishing industry, which it argues has been devastated by the Common Fisheries Policy, with potential value of £6.3 billion to the UK economy.

## Economy and Taxation

The fiscal approach emphasizes tax reduction without increasing overall taxation. Proposed measures include raising the personal income tax allowance to £13,500, increasing the 40% tax threshold to £55,000, and raising inheritance tax thresholds to £500,000 per individual. Business support includes 20% rate cuts for premises under £50,000 rateable value. The manifesto opposes tax avoidance by large corporations and promises to close EU-related loopholes.

## Healthcare

The NHS would receive £9 billion additional annual funding by 2021/22, with £2 billion more for social care. Key proposals include lifting medical school training caps from 7,500 to 10,000 places, covering tuition fees for medical students who commit to ten years NHS service, and restoring nurse bursaries. Mental health spending would increase by £500 million annually, with maximum 28-day waiting times for referrals. Foreign nationals would need five consecutive years of tax contributions before accessing non-urgent NHS services.

## Immigration

The manifesto proposes reducing net migration to zero over five years through an Australian-style points-based system applying equally to all applicants regardless of origin. A moratorium on unskilled immigration is proposed for five years post-Brexit. Integration policies include proposals to disband sharia councils and ban face coverings in public places. Work visas would prioritize those earning minimum £30,000 annually.

## Education

Educational reforms include opening grammar schools in every town, with transfer examinations available up to age sixteen. Tuition fees would be abolished for STEM subjects for students committing to five years UK work. Vocational training would be enhanced through German-style dual education systems combining classroom learning with workplace training.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would reach genuine 2% GDP plus £1 billion annually, with 20,000 additional armed forces personnel. The manifesto proposes 20,000 more police officers, 7,000 prison officers, and 4,000 border staff. Stop and Search powers would be fully restored. A new Veterans' Administration would be created as an independent body to support former service personnel.

## Housing

A Housing Development Corporation would deliver up to 100,000 factory-built modular homes annually, sold to first-time buyers under 40 with prices under £100,000 for two-bedroom homes. These would be owner-occupied only, with resale restricted to the Corporation at cost plus inflation.

## Constitutional Reform

The House of Lords would be abolished and replaced with an English Parliament of 375 members using proportional representation. The House of Commons would be reduced to 325 members. Binding citizen-initiated referenda would be held every two years on petitions gaining sufficient signatures.

## Foreign Aid

The foreign aid budget would be reduced from 0.7% to 0.2% of Gross National Income, saving approximately £10 billion annually for domestic services. The Department for International Development would be closed, with remaining aid administered through the Foreign Office.

## Fiscal Summary

Total projected savings by 2021/22 reach £35 billion annually, derived from ending EU contributions, reducing foreign aid, cancelling HS2, and reforming the Barnett Formula. These funds would support the spending commitments across health, defence, policing, and tax reductions outlined throughout the document.
